cold flow gas can penetrate deep into the potential of galaxies, that this cold gas can dominate the growth of disks in low-mass galaxies, and that the presence of a hot halo in more massive galaxies does not prevent the penetration of cold flow gas.

the role of cold flows and their impact on the assembly of disk galaxies, including their stellar disks and their interstellar medium (ISM).

understanding the role of gas accreted from the intergalactic medium (IGM) in the formation of galaxies and their stellar disks, and in particular with the role of gas that remains cold during its journey from the IGM to the galaxy.
the role of the cold gas accretion in galaxy formation, and how it can explain the observed properties of galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cold flows are an important ingredient in the formation of galaxy disks.
the cold flows are the dominant mechanism of the gas accretion in low-mass galaxies and the dominant mechanism of gas accretions in the central regions of massive galaxies.
, although hot gas is the main component of the gas in the halo of a galaxy, cold flows are the main driver of the growth of the stellar disk of galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cold flow accretion is a major component in the assembly of galaxies, with cold flow accreted gas dominating SF in low-mass galaxies and playing a significant role in the growth of the stellar disk of higher-mass galaxies at early times.
cold flows dominate the gas accretion onto galaxies and are the main driver of SF at all times.

the standard model for the growth of disks, which relies on the cooling of a hot halo, is only a good approximation for massive, early-type galaxies, while for lower mass galaxies and for early-type galaxies at higher redshift, cold flows play a significant role in the growth of their disks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard model of SF in galaxy disks is incomplete.
cold flows are a significant component of gas accreted onto galaxies, and they can be the dominant source of gas for the growth of the galaxy disk at all redshifts.
the standard picture of hot halo accretion is insufficient for understanding the formation of galaxies.
